### Bug Analysis

#### Bug Scenario Description
The issue is that the screen reader cannot read the label of the radio button in the React version of the Carbon Design System, while it works correctly in the vanilla HTML version. The problem is observed when using assistive technologies like VoiceOver or JAWS.

#### Bug Root Cause
The root cause of the issue is the presence of the `aria-label` attribute in the React component, which is not needed and is interfering with the screen reader's ability to read the label text correctly. In the vanilla HTML, the label is correctly associated with the input via the `for` attribute, which is missing in the React version due to the unnecessary `aria-label`.

### Bug Location
The bug is located in the `RadioButton.js` file where the `aria-label` attribute is being set on the label element.

### Patch to Fix the Bug

```javascript
### packages/react/src/components/RadioButton/RadioButton.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
        <label
          htmlFor={this.uid}
          className={`${prefix}--radio-button__label`}
          aria-label={labelText}>
=======
        <label
          htmlFor={this.uid}
          className={`${prefix}--radio-button__label`}>
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

### Explanation
- **Search Block**: The code block where the `aria-label` attribute is being set on the `label` element.
- **Replace Block**: Removed the `aria-label` attribute to ensure the screen reader can correctly read the label text associated with the radio button.
